title: Welcome, Thou Victor in the Strife
description: Welcome, Thou Victor in the Strife in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Benjamin Schmolck wrote these words in German. Catherine Winkworth's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 228.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Wel-come, Thou Vic-tor in the strife, Wel-come from out the cave! To day we tri-umph in Thy life A-round Thine emp-ty grave.

lines: Welcome, Thou Victor in the strife,
Welcome from out the cave!
To-day we triumph in Thy life
Around Thine empty grave.
Our enemy is put to shame,
His short-lived triumph o’er;
Our God is with us, we exclaim;
We fear our foe no more.
The dwellings of the just resound
With songs of victory;
For in their midst Thou, Lord, art found
And bringest peace with Thee.
O let Thy conquering banner wave
O’er hearts Thou makest free;
And point the path that from the grave
Leads heavenward up to Thee.
We bury all our sin and crime
Deep in our Savior’s tomb
And seek the treasure there that time
And change can ne’er consume.
Fearless we lay us in the tomb
And sleep the night away;
For Thou art there to break the gloom
And call us back to-day.

licence: Public domain: Benjamin Schmolck died in 1737; Catherine Winkworth died in 1878.
credits: Words by Benjamin Schmolck (1672–1737), translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
